observations: Two large automotive engines with attached transmissions are shown.
The engine on the left has a silver valve cover with 'PORSCHE' clearly embossed on it.
The left engine features a plastic intake manifold with eight runners, identifying it as a V8 engine.
The engine on the right has a black ribbed intake manifold and appears to be a similar V8 configuration.
Wiring harnesses and some sensors are visible but appear disconnected and tangled.
The engines are stored on a dirty, oil-stained floor in a workshop or scrap yard environment.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical condition (e.g., seized, low compression, or damaged internals).
risks.proof: A video showing the engine being turned over by the crankshaft or a compression test report.

risks.risk: Exact model year and displacement (e.g., 2008-2010 vs 2011-2017).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine identification code or serial number stamped on the engine block.

risks.risk: Completeness of the engine assembly (missing accessories like alternator, starter, or AC compressor).
risks.proof: Photos of the engine from all four sides showing all bolt-on accessories.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a bare long block without accessories.

proof_requests: Photo of the engine identification code stamped on the block to confirm the exact model and year.
Video of the engine being turned over manually to ensure it is not seized.
Clear photos of all sides of the engine to verify which accessories are included.
Confirmation if the transmission shown is included in the price.
response.reason: The engine is clearly identified as a Porsche V8 by the branding on the valve cover. It matches the Porsche Cayenne V8 engines in the comparables and is priced at the worst case (older model) until proven otherwise.
